Subject: Economic buyer & procurement next steps — Lumen Tech

Hi Grace / Elliot —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking through Lumen's evaluation goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Key decision criteria: (1) predictable per-token/unit cost at scale, (2) <100ms 95th pct latency for our summary endpoints, (3) enterprise-grade data controls (VPC/KMS) and auditable logs.
- Timeline: you said finance is targeting a Q2 commit and procurement/legal review will need to finish by ~May 10.
- Open items we need to close to get a formal quote: confirmed economic buyer, budget owner, expected steady-state RPS/concurrency, and any required security evidence (SOC2, RFP/RFI items).

Attached: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (placeholder SOW) and Security_RFI_answers.xlsx (answers to the security questions we discussed).

Ask: can you introduce the budget owner / economic buyer and procurement contact so we can align pricing + procurement checklist? If helpful, we can propose a 30-min follow-up that includes the budget owner and procurement to map approvals and next steps. 

Proposed times (PST):
- Tue Apr 6, 10:00-10:30 or
- Wed Apr 7, 14:00-14:30

If those don't work, share 2 options that include the budget owner.

Thanks — I'll loop in Rishi (pricing) and Vivek (security) for the follow-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

- I'm the product lead owning the use case, but the budget owner is Michael Reyes (Head of Engineering) — mreyes@lumentech.com.
- The economic buyer is Susan Park (CFO) — susan.park@lumentech.com (she'll want a short exec summary).
- Procurement/Legal handle the SOC2/audit questions. Please route procurement questions to procurement@lumentech.com.

On volume: current expectation is ~20 requests/sec steady state for the summarization endpoint with short bursts up to ~150 concurrent requests during our nightly batch jobs.

For pricing, can you provide a ballpark (list price range) that we can use to justify the business case to Michael and Susan? A 1-2 sentence exec summary for Susan would be helpful.

Also — we can do the 30-min follow-up next week. I'm copying Michael on my reply (he's not on this thread yet) — Michael, can you join a short call to validate budget timing?

Thanks,

Hi all —

Quick exec summary for Susan (CFO): Redwood offers predictable, production-grade LLM inference with transparent unit economics; typical enterprise customers see 30-50% lower per-token cost vs. naive single-instance hosting through batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles. We support dedicated/reserved options for predictable monthly commits.

Ballpark pricing (very rough, for sizing only):
- Consumption (pay-as-you-go): $0.012-$0.03 per 1k tokens (depends on model family and quantization).
- Reserved (committed monthly capacity): effective unit price can be 25-45% lower for 6-12 month commitments; example: $0.007-$0.018 per 1k tokens.

To prepare a formal quote I need: expected monthly token volume (or steady-state RPS + avg tokens per call) and desired SLA/latency targets. Michael — can you share a ballpark expected monthly tokens or confirm the ~20 rps steady-state / bursts to 150 concurrency?

I'll draft a short 2-paragraph summary and attach a quote template for Marissa to circulate.

—Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa / Rishi / Vivek —

Thanks for the materials. Procurement will need the following to start our legal review: 
- SOC 2 Type II report (or SOC 2 letter)
- Data retention and deletion policy (how logs and payloads are stored/retained)
- Data flow diagram and inventory of subprocessors
- Standard MSA / proposed terms (we'll markup in DocuSign).

We can join a 30-min alignment call next week. Please provide the SOC2 report and the short answers deck you referenced. Also include your standard SLAs and security contact for questions. We'll respond with our redlines and a proposed schedule after review.
